2e51cd29cb5d.text: 1. Has the team discovered their first potential customers and identified any unmet needs not yet covered by other existing solutions?

d42de35494b1.text: Our first proposed customers are banana exporters and packing houses, with research institutes, farmers' associations and cooperatives as the likely payers. Interviews at the Taoyuan station, with farmers' associations, facility farms and the Taiwan Banana Research Institute confirmed the gap: there is no monitoring beyond looking at the crop. An instrumentation professional told us the barrier to on-site testing is trained personnel and lab infrastructure, not instrument price, so the unmet need is a fast, on-site screening layer that flags samples for lab confirmation.

a055aebb1341.text: 2. Has the team shown that their solution is possible, scalable and inventive?

949ab27c0cc6.text: Scalable: the receptor cartridge is swappable, so the same reader can target other odors, starting with banana and extending to mango and tea. Inventive: a living receptor layer combined with a fly-brain-inspired classifier that traces to our advisors' published research (Science Advances, 2025). We have not yet shown selectivity and long-term stability with our own data.

74c87969f9d7.text: 3. Has the team presented logical product development plans with realistic milestones, timelines, resources and risks?

af776616a7ac.text: We plan three phases to 2031: Validate (hardware acceptance criteria and an end-to-end demo), Pilot (exporters and institutions, ending in documented willingness to pay or a letter of intent), and Scale (multi-site banana, then mango and tea). The NT$3.0M starting capital covers roughly 9–12 months against Year-1 spend of NT$3.08M, and modeled rounds leave a gap of about NT$4.3M over three years. Main risks are hardware validation, buyer skepticism, GCaMP licensing and runway, each with a mitigation in the risk analysis.

6f5b1ec60704.text: 4. Has the team outlined the skills, capabilities and stakeholders required to be credible in developing their solution further?

a2f69ec2a6bc.text: The four-person team covers hardware, systems integration, dry-lab machine learning and wet-lab receptor work, advised by Prof. Chung-Chuan Lo and Prof. Ching-Che Charng, whose published mushroom-body research underlies our classifier. We respond with risk tiers plus lab confirmation, a tool that supports inspectors rather than replacing them, opt-in data sharing and institutional biosafety oversight.

5653193df85e.text: Plant disease and post-harvest spoilage cost the food system enormously. The FAO and the International Plant Protection Convention estimate that pests destroy up to 40% of global crops each year, at a cost of about US$220 billion [1]. Even after harvest, roughly 13–14% of food produced is lost between harvest and retail [2]. Bananas show the problem clearly: Fusarium wilt (Panama disease) is a recurring threat to global banana production [3], and in Taiwan we estimate that fungal-disease-related loss reaches about NT$3.51 billion a year, around 33.6% of the sector's NT$10.445 billion annual output value (team estimate).

de075efd7080.text: The tools used to catch these problems today fall into two groups. Visual inspection is fast but sees only symptoms, by which time disease has often spread or the batch has been mixed with healthy stock. Laboratory assays such as PCR and GC-MS are accurate but slow and impractical to run across a whole shipment, and, as an analytical-instrumentation professional told us, the real barrier is not instrument price but the trained personnel and lab infrastructure they require. Electronic noses could fill the gap, yet the chief science officer of an established domestic electronic-nose company told us that almost no commercial electronic nose has genuinely high selectivity, and that the sensing element itself, not the electronics or algorithms, is the bottleneck.

80d4f3c98265.text: We considered several applications, including mold detection in stored food, pathogen VOCs and origin verification. Mentor reviews and an industry interview pushed us to start from a single economically quantifiable use. We therefore chose early disease detection in Taiwan's banana export chain as our beachhead , with coffee and tea as later markets. Throughout, we describe the tool as rapid risk screening that recommends laboratory confirmation, because a VOC signal is not the same claim as a safety verdict.

5c10bb683388.text: Post-harvest quality control today relies on two disconnected approaches. Visual and manual sampling is fast but catches disease mainly once it is visible, and it depends on individual inspector experience. A researcher at the Taoyuan improvement station told us that there is currently no monitoring method beyond looking at the crop. Laboratory assays are accurate but destructive, and they need trained personnel and laboratory infrastructure, which makes them hard to apply across a full shipment. What is missing is a fast, non-destructive, on-site screening step that tells staff which samples deserve a laboratory test. That is the gap AeroSense aims to fill.

e7e0616244ae.text: AeroSense 1.0 is a portable, cartridge-based reader that exposes a sample's gas to engineered live-cell wells and reads their fluorescence. It is designed to return a disease-risk tier for a sample, with a target of minutes rather than hours (not yet measured end to end). Ripeness forecasting and quality grading are planned extensions and are not built yet.

f12c0e81a5f1.text: An operator loads a headspace gas sample into the inlet of a four-well cartridge matched to the target crop and disease, then starts a run from a phone interface. An ESP32 microcontroller drives four blue LEDs (about 468 nm) at distinct modulation frequencies (41, 67, 89 and 113 Hz), exciting HEK293 cells that express an olfactory receptor (OR/Orco) and a GCaMP6 calcium reporter. One shared photodiode, a transimpedance amplifier and a 16-bit ADC capture the fluorescence, and a digital lock-in separates the four channels from background noise. A recognition layer inspired by the fly mushroom body's PN–KC–MBON circuit then classifies the pattern. So far, that layer has been tested only on public metal-oxide sensor datasets, not on AeroSense cell signals.

d597991ee50a.text: The aim is a decision-ready read-out rather than a raw signal: a risk tier and a recommended next step, such as setting a batch aside for laboratory confirmation. It is a screening layer, not a laboratory replacement and not a safety verdict. Because the cartridge is swappable, the same base device could in principle be redeployed to other targets by developing new cartridges and models. Banana is the first target, and other crops remain hypotheses.

bcf11db142c9.text: The cartridges use HEK293, a standard mammalian cell line, with insect olfactory receptors expressed in it, so no live insects are involved. The cells are held in sealed wells, and the biosafety requirements for partner sites will be confirmed with institutional guidance before any field deployment.

6903fc948c4f.text: Positive impacts. AeroSense aims to reduce post-harvest agricultural loss and the economic and environmental cost of discarded produce. By pricing on a usage basis rather than a large capital outlay, the platform aims to give smaller exporters and cooperatives — not only large, well-resourced agribusinesses — access to a screening capability that today is effectively limited to buyers who can afford lab-grade testing. Over time, a growing multi-crop VOC dataset could help standardize quality grading across a currently inconsistent, judgment-based system, benefiting both producers (fairer, more transparent grading) and consumers (more reliable food-safety assurance).

c784dff679fd.text: Risks to manage. As with any automated risk-classification system, an over-trusted "risk score" could lead a partner to under-inspect a shipment the model misses (a false negative). This is precisely why the team designed the output as a risk tier with escalation guidance rather than a binary pass/fail — a decision informed directly by our public survey finding that false negatives are the least-tolerated failure mode among respondents. Broader deployment of an AI-driven agricultural sensing platform also carries a data-governance responsibility for the VOC and lot-level data collected from partner sites. Our current plan is to keep data project-scoped by default and to share only aggregated, anonymized data for model improvement with explicit partner opt-in — stated here as a policy plan , not yet a built and independently audited system.
